chapter: Chicago radio, Whiteman and courting Mildred
title: Joining Whiteman's vaudeville unit and marrying Mildred
summary: Neither wanted to leave Chicago for New York, but Whiteman asked him to join the vaudeville show; he and Mildred married on the road, with Trumbauer as best man.

story.theme_name: Meeting, marrying and raising a family
story.community_name: Meeting, courting and marrying: musicians' love lives

blocks.x: -- I mean the very thought of Whiteman going to New York, I know they were going to leave Chicago, I mean Mildred didn't like the idea and I know I didn't.
You didn't. You didn't want to go East?
No.
Cause life was good in Chicago?

And -- so I don't know, I'd done a few things with Paul and so he just walked in one day and said, why don't you do that slap thing with me in the vaudeville? Wanted me to go in vaudeville and join the band. So I just
couldn't talk, really. It was just what I really wanted.
And -- yeah.
And studio work wasn't what I really wanted to do.
No, it was too --
Not really.
-- cut and dried --
Yeah, so I went with him. I don't know how long I was with him, we went on the road, went and played theaters, it was very --
Had you and Mildred married then?
Not yet.
No.
And --
That was --
Just before -- we got married on the road, someplace -- we got -- out of Buffalo, I think we were in Shay's, Buffalo. Don't remember.
Yeah. Anybody know you were going to get married, or did you just go off and get married?
Well I think we both felt it coming on.
Yeah, but I mean nobody in the band, though
Yeah, I think so -- I think that.
Who was your best man or do you remember?
Frankie. (laughs)
Oh, it was Frankie? Oh, that's good. That's nice.
Frankie Trumbauer.
Yeah, that's nice, that's very nice. What did Whiteman do you -- for you, did he he celebrate or anything?
Yeah they took us to -- course it was during Prohibition, took us over to Canada --
Oh, yeah. Oh, they did?
Yeah. It was kind of nice, celebration over in Canada, with champagne and all.
